fields.v: Partly (0.5): main conclusions follow from the tables, but RQ1 claims the Individual setting outperforms Global and PRD 'across all evaluated repositories' although Table 3 shows exceptions (e.g. Sonnet 4.5 Conan 8 vs 10 Global; Gemini 3 Pro Haystack 5 vs 7 Global), and 'significantly inflated' is claimed without a test
fields.quote: comparisons on the Mini dataset reveal a consistent trend where the standard “Individual PR” setting outperforms the “Global” (conversational) and “PRD-based” settings across all evaluated repositories.
fields.why: The '15% to 25% across all LLMs' sentence is about the Lite results (Table 7), where it holds; the overstatement is the 'across all evaluated repositories' claim on Mini, so the score stays Partly but the reason should change.
fields.doubt: A frase dos '15% a 25%' refere-se ao Lite (Tabela 7, pág. 15), onde se confirma (cerca de 18 a 24 pp). O exagero real é 'em todos os repositórios' no Mini: a Tabela 3 tem exceções (Sonnet Conan 8 vs 10). A nota fica Parcial; só muda a justificação.

fields.v: Inconsistencies: model named 'Gemini 3 Flash' in Tables 3 and 7 but 'Gemini 2.5 Flash' in the Global/PRD rows of Table 9 and in the Aider tables 10-12; Section 4.1 assigns Gemini 3 Flash and GPT-5.1 Codex Mini to the Lite split only, but Table 3 (Mini) reports them too; RQ1 claim that the Individual setting outperforms Global and PRD 'across all evaluated repositories' (Mini) vs Table 3 exceptions (e.g. Sonnet 4.5 Conan 8 Individual vs 10 Global; Gemini 3 Pro Haystack 5 vs 7 and DVC 2 vs 3 Global); the '15% to 25%' decrease 'across all LLMs' refers to Lite Table 7, where it holds (17.8-24.3 pp); Table 8 Codex Mini Individual and Global averages identical (87.16 / 56.15); Table 12 'Local' per-repository values repeat the Table 11 PRD row, yet its averages differ (P2P 28.18/57.61, F2P 20.82/37.76 vs 98.91/58.20, 5.35/29.12), and Table 12 caption repeats Table 11's; 'Gemini 3.0 Pro' vs 'Gemini 3 Pro'; Table 1 says 48.7% of tasks have interdependent PRs while the text calls dependency signals 'quite rare'. Values from Tables 3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 (pp. 7, 15, 18); Table 12 averages rebuilt from the jumbled text by position (each row ends with its average P2P, then a line with the two F2P averages, as in Tables 9 and 11); per-model task counts summed from Table 3 columns. Data: SWE-STEPS-mini shared as a zip with the submission; dataset and code to be released (on acceptance). Pre-registration: not stated. Programming language: Python
fields.quote: When scaling the evaluation, models such as Gemini 3 Flash see a degradation from 56.52% in the Individual setting to just 36.59% in the Global setting. Across all LLMs, we observe a consistent performance decrease ranging between 15% to 25% when statefulness is introduced.
fields.why: The listed inconsistency compares a Lite claim with Mini numbers; on Lite (Table 7) the drops are 17.8-24.3 pp, so it is not an inconsistency, while the 'across all evaluated repositories' claim is.
fields.doubt: A inconsistência dos '15-25%' compara uma frase sobre o Lite com números do Mini. No Lite (Tabela 7) as quedas estão entre 17,8 e 24,3 pp. Propõe-se trocar esse ponto pela exceção real ('todos os repositórios' vs Tabela 3). Confirma na pág. 8 e decide.
